issueContext.body:
## Problem

Profile editing components each manage mutation coordination, query ownership, stale responses, and focus lifetimes. Correctness depends on repeated guards spread across inline fields, picture settings, and alias settings. The existing tests cover many cases, but adding another editing flow requires understanding the same concurrency rules in several places.

This is a maintenance concern identified during #235, not a newly reproduced user-facing failure.

## Scope

Design a small Profile editing interface that owns the common mutation and owner-cache lifecycle. Move shared behavior behind it incrementally, preserving context-specific commands and presentation in each component. Keep DOM focus behavior close to the UI where it depends on actual user interaction; do not build a generic form framework.

Start with one editing flow, prove the interface through behavior tests, then migrate the picture and alias flows only where they share the same rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- Signing out, switching owners, or removing/recreating an owner query cannot let a late mutation restore stale Profile data or write into another owner's cache.
- Concurrent edits retain the existing serialization/version-conflict behavior. Failures preserve recoverable drafts and give the user an explicit next action.
- Navigation/unmount during a successful mutation updates only the still-valid owner cache and does not restore an obsolete component's focus.
- Dialog cancellation, retry, keyboard submission, and focus restoration preserve current behavior and respect intervening user focus changes.
- Components consume a deliberate public interface instead of repeating query-identity and mutation-coordination guards. Avoid wrappers whose interface merely reproduces the component's existing complexity.
- Existing behavioral regressions remain green, new guarantees have focused tests, and the deployed Profile editing flows pass browser validation.

## Starting points

- `apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-inline-field.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-picture-settings.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-alias-settings.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/hooks/use-owner-profile.ts`
- `apps/web/test/components/profile-bootstrap.test.tsx` and the related Profile component tests

Preserve Profile API contracts, displayed behavior, and the current owner-clearing guarantees. Select the exact module placement after examining the existing hooks and cache helpers.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Verification outcome

The requested shared Profile editing lifecycle is already implemented. Closing this maintenance request as already implemented, using the triage workflow's `wontfix` disposition for redundant requests. This is not a rejection of its behavior or a new out-of-scope policy.

I checked both threads named by the maintainer:

- `e340dd35-b76e-495b-ad61-13f37cbb9071` implemented #396 in [PR #398](https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/pull/398), merged on October 15. It concentrates picture-session ownership, captured versions, cancellation, retry, and conflict recovery behind the picture workflow. It completes the picture-specific portion of this request.
- `88926f84-6e5f-4bca-8c24-c8544af15e8f` implements #397 in [PR #399](https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/pull/399), still open at verification. That change centralizes static image processing policy across worker and fallback. It is separate from mutation/cache concurrency and is not needed to satisfy this issue.

The common coordination was introduced earlier in `b95a5184`, with subsequent synchronous admission and saved-query coordination changes. Inline fields, picture editing, and aliases now use the shared `useOwnerProfileMutation` boundary. Saved Profile query identity controls late cache publication; request ownership is captured at submission; UI feedback has a separate lifetime; command availability is checked by the accepting operation. Field and picture workflows preserve drafts and version-conflict recovery while DOM focus handling stays in the UI.

### Current implementation

- [Shared query/mutation lifecycle](https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/blob/8e32ff9fb842c51ec08ade9f57a668b53563d269/apps/web/src/features/profile-management/adapters/query.ts)
- [Field editor adapter](https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/blob/8e32ff9fb842c51ec08ade9f57a668b53563d269/apps/web/src/features/profile-editor/adapters/react.ts)
- [Picture editor adapter](https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/blob/8e32ff9fb842c51ec08ade9f57a668b53563d269/apps/web/src/features/picture-editor/adapters/react.ts)
- [Alias settings](https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/blob/8e32ff9fb842c51ec08ade9f57a668b53563d269/apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-alias-settings.tsx)

### Validation

Verified against main commit `8e32ff9fb842c51ec08ade9f57a668b53563d269`. The triage checkout lacks installed dependencies, so I ran the focused tests in the completed #396 worktree at `a8835476`. Both commits have the identical Git tree `7fcad433f616259c85d8efebea3d2d5437484436`.

```sh
make test-focused PACKAGE=web ARGS='test/features/profile-mutation-adapter.dom.test.tsx test/features/profile-editor.test.ts test/features/profile-management.test.ts test/features/picture-editor-workflow.test.ts test/components/profile/profile-inline-field.dom.test.tsx test/components/profile/profile-picture-settings.dom.test.tsx test/components/profile-bootstrap.dom.test.tsx'
```

Result: **7 files passed, 131 tests passed**. Coverage includes original-cache publication after navigation, replacement-query protection, changed owners, synchronous competing-command rejection, conflict/draft behavior, and component lifetimes/focus regressions. No new code was needed.

The #396 thread additionally records full local `make ci` passing, all five real browser journeys passing, and all three hosted CI checks plus Codex reviews passing for the merged implementation. I did not repeat deployed browser E2E during this triage. No remaining implementation gap was found in the issue's acceptance criteria.

## Parent

#39

## What to build

Let users discover Profiles through fuzzy Handle, active-alias, and Display name search, then select a Profile in the wallpaper filter UI to run an exact Profile-ID wallpaper query. Keep Profile data in the Profile index rather than denormalizing it into wallpaper documents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GraphQL exposes cursor-paginated Profile search over current Handles, active/expiring aliases, and Display names.
- [ ] Ranking prioritizes exact current Handle, Handle prefix, exact alias, alias prefix, Display name phrase/prefix, then fuzzy Display name.
- [ ] Current Handles outrank aliases and Profile ID is a stable pagination tiebreaker.
- [ ] Biography is not searched and public Profile results do not enumerate alias lists.
- [ ] If duplicate projected claims appear, exact resolution chooses the highest claim generation.
- [ ] The web filter provides fuzzy Profile selection and stores/submits the selected Profile ID.
- [ ] Wallpaper filtering remains an exact ownership-ID query; Profile fields are not copied into wallpaper documents.
- [ ] Tests cover ranking, aliases through expiry, cursor stability, duplicate claims, selection UX, and wallpaper results.

## Blocked by

- #172
- #173
- #169

comments.body:
Implemented in small test-driven commits through `959cfe5` on `t3code/implement-user-profiles`.

- Added cursor-paginated `searchProfiles` with fixed ranking tiers, active-alias expiry checks, stable Profile-ID ties, bounded inputs, and query-bound signed cursors. Optional leading `@`, whitespace, and case normalize consistently. Biography is excluded; aliases remain private.
- Added the Profile picker with current identity/picture, pagination, loading/error/empty recovery, saved selections, and stale-request protection. The URL and wallpaper requests carry only the selected exact Profile ID. Clearing preserves other filters; returning to the beginning resets only the cursor.
- Made filters reachable on mobile and kept filtering available during wallpaper loading/errors. Wallpaper documents retain ownership IDs without Profile-field duplication.

Validation:

- Gateway: **184 passed**, one existing skip; actual TypeScript, scoped lint, and format passed. Integration tests use real OpenSearch and cover ranking, expiry, cursor stability/security, duplicate claims, privacy, and exact wallpaper ownership.
- Web: **423 passed** across 38 files, including real-router/GraphQL-transport navigation tests. Node TypeScript and lint passed (one existing lint warning). Actual app TypeScript has the same **72 pre-existing diagnostics**, with no added or removed diagnostics after normalized comparison.
- `agent-browser`: desktop and 390px mobile checks passed for filter access, keyboard selection, second-page selection, exact outgoing IDs, combined/cleared filters, unavailable saved Profiles, lookup/search retries, pasted Handles, and cursor recovery. Used the real frontend with a controlled API fixture; backend behavior is covered separately by integration tests. No browser errors or horizontal overflow.
- Independent Standards and Spec reviews both **PASS** at `959cfe5` with zero remaining findings.

All work for this subissue is committed. #175 remains for retention, followed by final umbrella checks.

## Parent

#243

## What to build

A signed-in User chooses a static JPEG, PNG, or WebP in the existing Profile picture dialog, frames it in a square crop, and applies the change. Browser processing produces the small canonical image before upload while the page remains responsive and cancellable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reuse the existing dialog. Source selection changes its contents into the editor; processing never opens another modal.
- [ ] Fetch the effective User picture policy before processing. Validate supported source formats with a clear error; do not reject a local static source solely because of compressed file size or megapixel count.
- [ ] Offer a fixed 1:1 crop, drag positioning, an accessible keyboard-operable zoom slider, and Reset. Display a circular preview mask while exporting a square asset without baked-in circular clipping.
- [ ] Clamp movement so the source covers the entire crop at every allowed zoom and position. Preserve transparent source pixels without adding padding outside the source bounds.
- [ ] Cap zoom before the selected crop represents less than 64 by 64 source pixels. If its initial region is already smaller, disable further zoom, show a quality warning, and still allow Apply.
- [ ] Selecting a replacement unsaved source replaces the previous selection immediately and resets crop and zoom without a confirmation dialog.
- [ ] Apply source orientation before editing/cropping. Produce a predictable sRGB SDR WebP at the policy's canonical dimensions, initially 512 by 512, with static encoding starting at quality 85. Preserve alpha and strip private and unrelated source metadata.
- [ ] Perform decode and transformation outside the main UI thread when supported. A fallback yields sufficiently for cancellation and UI updates to remain responsive.
- [ ] Show a small loader and accessible X cancel button inside the same dialog during processing. Cancellation stops outstanding processing and prevents partial or late processing results from being uploaded.
- [ ] Apply processes and uploads only the canonical result through the dedicated authenticated picture command, independent of unrelated Profile saves. Never upload or retain the large original.
- [ ] Close the dialog only after User accepts the upload and publish the accepted authoritative Profile response. Decode, processing, and upload failures show a clear error and retain source and crop for another attempt.
- [ ] Release UI-owned worker work and object URLs when appropriate. A superseded selection or abandoned editing session cannot receive a late processing result or submit the wrong source.
- [ ] Preserve the existing nested confirmation for picture removal and generated-avatar selection. Do not introduce rotation, flipping, arbitrary aspect ratios, forced camera capture, or a general form refactor.

## Blocked by

- #337 - Expose effective Profile picture policy and enforce canonical static uploads

## Testing

- Use a complete static browser E2E journey through the actual editor, worker, upload command, and updated Profile picture. Cover pointer positioning, keyboard slider control, Reset, and browser-dependent cancellation.
- Use focused public-interface tests for crop geometry, clamping, minimum source-region zoom, and the below-64-pixel case.
- Frontend adapter tests cover source replacement, policy/decode/processing/upload failures, retained edits, outgoing processed bytes and expected version, and late completion after cancellation or session replacement.
- Use real fixtures to verify orientation, transparency, metadata removal, canonical dimensions, and sRGB SDR output. Use bounded completion waits without fixed sleeps or retries that hide failure.

## Scope

This is an approved implementation slice of #243. It produces one canonical SDR Profile picture Asset and preserves User ownership, immutable identity, current-picture availability, and the existing removal/import lifecycle. Generic Media rendition delivery and HDR conversion are separate work. The accepted HDR policy in #270 and its Media processing ownership leave this SDR browser path intact; neither that work nor #237 is an additional blocker unless listed explicitly.

## Parent

#39

## What to build

Let a signed-in User change their Profile Handle while preserving link continuity. The User service atomically claims the normalized Handle, enforces reserved names and the seven-day cooldown, turns the previous Handle into an alias, and projects canonical routing changes to GraphQL and web.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Handle changes use the explicit authenticated command and optimistic Profile version.
- [ ] Handles enforce lowercase ASCII letters, digits, single hyphens, configurable 1–30 length, and technical reserved names.
- [ ] Current Handles and aliases share one unique PostgreSQL claim namespace.
- [ ] Concurrent claims permit exactly one winner and assign a monotonically increasing claim generation.
- [ ] A successful change makes the previous current Handle an alias and records all transitions atomically.
- [ ] A Profile cannot change Handle more than once per seven days.
- [ ] Old and new public routes resolve and redirect to the new canonical Handle after projection.
- [ ] Settings explain validation, collision, cooldown, and successful redirect behavior.
- [ ] Tests cover normalization, reserved names, concurrency, cooldown, events, projection, and redirects.

## Blocked by

- #166

comments.body:
Implemented #170 in small committed red/green increments.

- Authenticated, versioned Handle changes validate normalized Handles, reserve claims atomically, enforce the seven-day cooldown, and preserve former Handles as aliases.
- Competing claims have one winner; outbox failures roll back state and claims. Complete snapshots preserve aliases across Display name edits and owner reads. Owners can promote a retained alias back to their current Handle after the cooldown.
- GraphQL returns HandleResolution with canonical routing information, resolves the highest matching claim generation, and keeps alias lists private. Existing Profile indexes receive additive alias mappings without losing documents.
- Settings preserve drafts on errors, distinguish collisions from stale edits, show cooldown timing, and adopt authoritative results immediately.
- Agent-browser verified normalized updates, collision/conflict feedback, canonical links, old-Handle redirects, and the mobile layout using the normal Clerk session and controlled REST/GraphQL fixtures.

The full specification review passed with no findings. Final verification details follow.

- Standards review also passed with no findings.
- User suite: **39 passed**; actual User, Events, and Gateway source/test TypeScript checks passed.
- Full web suite: **347 passed across 32 files**. Configured web check, Node project type check, changed-source lint, and diff checks passed.
- A direct web app/test TypeScript check reports **72 pre-existing diagnostics**. An isolated checkout of pre-#170 commit `3e2b4eb` reports the identical diagnostic multiset; this issue introduces none. This baseline limitation remains outside #170.
- Final Gateway Profile/OpenSearch regression: **23 passed**. Events regression: **53 passed**.

Completed through commit `50ef270`; working tree clean. All required #170 behavior is implemented, reviewed, and verified.

## Parent PRD

#35

## What to build

Migrate the gateway's pagination from offset-based (`from`/`size`) to OpenSearch's `search_after` cursor-based pagination. The public GraphQL API remains unchanged — cursors stay opaque (HMAC-signed base64url) — but internally they encode `search_after` values instead of integer offsets.

For unsorted queries, use `search_after: [wallpaperId]` as a deterministic tiebreaker. Update `CursorService` to encode/decode an array of values (strings, numbers) instead of a single offset integer. Update `WallpaperRepository.search()` to accept `searchAfter` instead of `from`. Update the resolver to pass `search_after` values from decoded cursors and encode new cursors from the last result's sort values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CursorService` encodes/decodes `search_after` values (array) instead of integer offsets
- [ ] `WallpaperRepository.search()` uses `search_after` instead of `from`/`size`
- [ ] Resolver passes `search_after` from decoded cursor and encodes new cursors from result sort values
- [ ] Forward pagination (`first` + `after`) works correctly
- [ ] Backward pagination (`last` + `before`) works correctly
- [ ] Unsorted queries use `search_after: [wallpaperId]` for deterministic ordering
- [ ] Public GraphQL API is unchanged — cursors remain opaque to clients
- [ ] Existing integration tests updated and passing
- [ ] HMAC signing and cursor expiration still enforced

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

## User stories addressed

- User story 10

standards.text:
# Project organization

Scope: module organization and shared testing principles apply project-wide. The backend architecture section applies only to backend applications and their supporting modules.

## Module organization

- All maintained code and scripts, including repository tooling and vendored code, must be owned by a pnpm workspace package. The root package may own repository-wide orchestration, scripts, and integration checks; a separate package is not required for every script.
- Each workspace declares its dependencies and exposes applicable build, lint, test, and type-check tasks through the standard package scripts. These tasks must participate in the shared Turbo task graph, with dependencies, inputs, outputs, and cache behavior declared for correct execution. Define only meaningful tasks; a package that exports TypeScript source does not need an empty build task.
- A backend capability lives under `src/capabilities/<name>/` and exposes a small interface through its `index.ts` entry point. External code and tests import only from that entry point. The entry names only the intended public contract: types, interfaces, service keys, errors, and deliberately public construction functions or layers. Put contract declarations in `contract.ts` and behavior, policy calculations, and layer construction in private implementation files. An entry may explicitly re-export a public layer or function from its implementation file; it must not contain the implementation or use wildcard exports. Avoid abstractions that merely delegate.
- Mechanically enforce architectural dependencies: package export maps protect package interfaces, while dependency-graph checks protect capability entry points, inward dependency direction, and acyclicity.
- Every deployable backend application opts in to the shared architecture check when created. An existing application opts in when it adopts capability architecture. The directories under `src/capabilities/` define capability ownership; do not duplicate that list in `quality.config.json`. The config declares other local boundaries and permitted external dependencies. Its `lint:architecture` package script invokes the shared checker. The repository lint pipeline runs that task through Turbo; direct package `lint` scripts cover their own lint commands. The application owner maintains its boundary configuration, while changes to the shared checker and its regression tests are repository tooling changes. See the [checker](../../scripts/check-architecture.mjs), [gateway configuration](../../apps/gateway/quality.config.json), [Turbo task graph](../../turbo.json), and [Make lint entry point](../../Makefile).
- Use shared packages for cohesive modules whose stable semantics are genuinely common to actual consumers, with a deliberate interface and clear ownership. Keep context-specific meanings local and accept small duplication when sharing would couple them; shared packages must not depend on deployable applications.
- Filename conventions must not impose mandatory architectural role suffixes.

## Backend architecture

- Each independently deployable backend application is one hexagon. Its capabilities are vertical, deep modules inside that hexagon; neither the monorepo, individual capabilities, nor shared packages are automatically separate hexagons.
- Domain and application code depend inward; driving and driven adapters translate external concerns at the application boundary.
- Strategic DDD is mandatory for backend capabilities. Every capability belongs to exactly one bounded context and uses its ubiquitous language in code, tests, ports, events, and documentation. A context may contain several capabilities, while an application should normally serve one context.
- Domain and persistence models remain private to their bounded context. Cross-context public contracts are translated into the receiving context's model; a shared domain kernel requires an explicit documented exception.
- Each application exclusively owns its private mutable persistence. Shared immutable assets may be consumed directly from object storage when every object has one owning producer, consumer permissions are limited to their needs, and lifecycle responsibility is explicit. Only the owner may delete an object, and changed content receives a new logical identity.

When designing backend behavior, follow [application and domain guidelines](application-and-domain.md). When exchanging facts between applications, follow [distributed contracts](distributed-interactions.md#contracts). For resources shared within an application, follow [composition and lifecycle ownership](composition-and-operations.md#configuration-and-lifecycle).

## Shared testing principles

- Tests cover each specified behavior, expected failure, domain invariant, and port guarantee at the narrowest public boundary that owns it. Repeat a scenario at a wider boundary only when that boundary introduces a distinct risk. The [telemetry testing policy](composition-and-operations.md#testing) qualifies this rule for backend instrumentation.
- Every maintained function must meet the configured CRAP threshold. CRAP is an implementation-risk backstop, not proof of behavioral completeness.
- Prefer controlled stateful adapters over mocks that assert incidental method order. Assert observable port effects; use an interaction assertion only when the interaction itself is part of the port contract.
- Tests are deterministic, independently runnable, and parallel-safe: control nondeterministic inputs, isolate test data and state, and await observable asynchronous conditions with bounded deadlines rather than fixed sleeps. Treat flakiness as a defect; retries must not conceal it.

For backend test boundaries, read the relevant subject: [capabilities and domain](application-and-domain.md#testing), [adapters](adapters.md#testing), or [composition and operations](composition-and-operations.md#testing). These backend test categories do not prescribe a frontend test architecture.

## Browser E2E testing

Browser E2E tests cover a small set of successful, complete user journeys through the web UI and real application services. They do not repeat the full behavioral matrix. Follow the [browser workspace README](../../apps/web-e2e/README.md) for setup and execution.

# Frontend design

Scope: browser application code and shared frontend/UI modules. The [project-wide module organization rules](project-organization.md#module-organization) also apply.

## State ownership

- Give each kind of state one authoritative owner. The query layer owns the saved server data and request activity it manages; the router owns URL state; the authentication provider owns authentication state; editors own unsaved drafts and editing sessions.
- Derive combined values such as command availability and `canSave` from their owners. Avoid synchronizing additional mutable copies of request activity between the query layer, an editor, and React.
- An editor's captured base value and version are intentional history. Preserve them while the user edits, and change them only when the editing policy explicitly adopts or rebases onto newer server data.

## Feature interfaces

- Cross-feature dependencies use deliberately public entries. Keep private implementation details private and feature dependencies acyclic.
- Designate effectful adapter entries explicitly. A file's placement in an adapter directory does not make it public.

## Command coordination

- Enforce shared command restrictions in the operation that accepts and executes the commands. Disabled controls communicate availability; they must not be the only enforcement.
- When overlapping commands are disallowed, check and reserve availability before yielding to asynchronous work. All callers subject to that restriction use the same coordination owner, which releases availability when the operation finishes.
- Choose rejection, queuing, or concurrency according to the intended behavior and scope the restriction to the affected resource. For example, name and picture updates for one Profile may share a restriction while updates to different Profiles proceed concurrently. Two submissions arriving before React renders disabled controls must still obey that policy.

## Request and UI lifetimes

- An accepted request retains its intended command and owner. Define whether it continues after navigation and where its result may be published.
- Separate cache publication from component feedback. A response may update its original valid cache after the editor unmounts; toasts, focus changes, and local feedback belong to the originating UI lifetime.
- Responses from an earlier session must not overwrite a replacement session's cache or update its UI. Identify request ownership independently of the current rendered component or a reused profile identifier.
- Release UI-owned timers and subscriptions when their owning UI lifetime ends. Late completions must respect that lifetime even when the underlying request continues.

## Testing

The [shared testing principles](project-organization.md#shared-testing-principles) apply. Select frontend test boundaries by the responsibility they exercise:

- Test calculations and workflows through their public interfaces.
- Test React/query integration for synchronization and lifecycle behavior.
- Use browser tests for behavior that depends on real focus, measurement, or animation. The [browser E2E policy](project-organization.md#browser-e2e-testing) governs complete journeys through real services.
- For complex editors, cover dirty-draft preservation, captured confirmations, competing commands, navigation, and session replacement where those behaviors apply. Assert the intended command and publication outcomes without depending on private implementation details.

# Backend application and domain

Scope: backend capabilities, their application-owned ports, domain policy, and tests.

## Effect and dependencies

- Effect is the required programming model for effectful application and domain operations, dependency composition, and resource lifecycles. Pure values and calculations remain ordinary TypeScript.
- Every injected port has an application-owned TypeScript interface and a colocated, namespaced Effect `Context.Service` key; adapters explicitly implement their port interfaces. Separate `Symbol.for(...)` tokens, TSyringe containers, and property injection are not used.
- Use Effect Layers to construct services and supply their dependencies. Resolve implementation dependencies during layer construction rather than exposing them as requirements of the port's operations. Private implementations may still use ordinary constructors; pure domain values and calculations do not need to become services.
- Application and domain code declare typed dependencies rather than using global service locators or creating or running their own runtimes. [Composition selects implementations and lifetimes](composition-and-operations.md#configuration-and-lifecycle); [driving adapters execute effects at transport boundaries](adapters.md#driving-adapters).

## Outcomes and failures

- Represent normal domain and application decisions, including absence, validation rejection, quota denial, and intentional no-ops, as explicit values. Use discriminated unions where callers must distinguish outcomes; do not introduce a result wrapper when the returned value already expresses the outcome.
- Represent technical failures that prevent an operation from completing as application-owned tagged errors in Effect's typed error channel. Unexpected defects and violated programmer assumptions remain defects, not ordinary application outcomes.
- Underlying causes may be retained as opaque diagnostic context on application-owned errors. Application and domain code must not inspect vendor errors, library validation details, or error-message text to make decisions.

For translation of external failures and safe responses, follow [adapter boundary translation](adapters.md#boundary-translation). For recording diagnostic context, follow [observability](composition-and-operations.md#observability).

## Ports and transactions

- Create application-owned ports only at genuine external-effect or technology boundaries. A port describes purposeful operations in the consuming capability's language and must not expose infrastructure or another bounded context's types. Opaque diagnostic causes follow the [failure policy](#outcomes-and-failures).
- A port states every observable guarantee on which the application relies. Production and controlled test adapters must satisfy the same contract.
- The application declares atomicity; adapters own transaction mechanics. Work that must commit together crosses one capability-scoped transactional port, expressed as a deep semantic operation or a scoped unit of work when decisions must occur inside the transaction.
- Raw transactions must not enter application code, transaction-scoped collaborators must not escape their scope, and separate ports must never be assumed to share a transaction. Independently transactional resources remain separate and external effects do not run as part of a database transaction.

For concurrent writes and persistence enforcement, follow [persistence adapters](adapters.md#persistence-adapters). For work spanning independent resources, follow [delivery reliability](distributed-interactions.md#delivery-reliability).

## Domain policy

- Each capability consistently chooses language-only DDD or tactical DDD. Introduce entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, domain services, and other tactical patterns only where they protect a real modeling need; `GLOSSARY.md` records language, not implementation patterns.
- Domain events are optional. Prefer explicit calls and transition results, do not use an internal event bus to hide control flow, and treat event sourcing as a separate architectural decision.
- Domain construction and transitions enforce business invariants. Internal code may rely on values that have crossed the structural and domain boundaries instead of repeatedly revalidating them. Invariants susceptible to concurrent or external writes also need [persistence enforcement](adapters.md#persistence-adapters).
- Application and domain policy authorize every protected operation. Authentication mechanisms must not leak inward, and caller-supplied ownership claims must not override the authenticated principal. [Driving adapters translate authentication](adapters.md#driving-adapters).
- Defaults and normalization have one owner. Checks that depend on their results must use the owner's resolved values rather than independently reproduce its rules.
- Bound caller-controlled quantities that determine resource consumption. Enforce limits at the boundary that owns the constrained work; defaults and cost estimates do not replace those limits. For example, a capability owns its maximum page size, while a GraphQL adapter owns protocol-specific query limits.

For capability/context placement and language ownership, follow [backend architecture](project-organization.md#backend-architecture).

## Testing

- Capability tests call a driving port and assert its result and declared driven-port effects using controlled adapters. They test the whole capability as the unit, not its internal classes. Test business outcomes at this boundary.
- Focused tests of complex pure domain logic are appropriate when they improve diagnosis or cheaply cover a substantial decision table; they need not duplicate capability tests.

Apply the [shared testing principles](project-organization.md#shared-testing-principles) and the [port guarantees above](#ports-and-transactions) when constructing controlled adapters. If the behavior belongs to a transport or external system, use [adapter tests](adapters.md#testing).

# Backend adapters

Scope: backend driving adapters, driven adapters, external input/output translation, and adapter tests.

## Boundary translation

- Translate incoming external contracts before they cross a driving port and translate outgoing local concepts after they cross a driven port.
- Treat external input as untrusted until an adapter parses and translates it into application-owned types. Adapters enforce structural contracts. Type or non-null assertions must not bypass validation.
- Translate validation failures into declared outcomes or typed errors before crossing ports; underlying library errors may be retained only as opaque diagnostic causes. Translate vendor failures into application-owned typed errors according to the [outcome and failure policy](application-and-domain.md#outcomes-and-failures).
- Integrate Promise- or callback-based libraries into Effect. Adapters implement the [application-owned port contract](application-and-domain.md#ports-and-transactions).

When input interpretation affects admission or execution, follow [ownership of defaults and resource bounds](application-and-domain.md#domain-policy). When handling technical failures, follow the [diagnostic telemetry requirements](composition-and-operations.md#observability). For client acquisition, cancellation, and cleanup, follow [configuration and lifecycle](composition-and-operations.md#configuration-and-lifecycle).

## Driving adapters

- Obtain inbound ports rather than concrete handlers and execute effects at the transport boundary.
- Authenticate callers and translate technical identity into an application-owned principal. [Application and domain policy own authorization](application-and-domain.md#domain-policy).
- Exhaustively translate declared outcomes and typed failures into transport behavior. Do not expose diagnostic causes in public responses.
- Apply security and admission controls to the operation identified by the driving adapter. Alternative external representations that resolve to the same operation must receive the same controls.

For broker consumers, also follow [distributed contracts and delivery reliability](distributed-interactions.md). For NATS publishers and consumers, follow [NATS and JetStream](nats.md).

## Public HTTP APIs

- REST error bodies and HTTP transport error bodies outside GraphQL responses use RFC 9457 Problem Details with a correct status code and an explicit, stable problem-type URI; `about:blank` is prohibited. WallpaperDB-specific types use `https://github.com/rafaeltab/wallpaperdb/blob/main/docs/problems/<type>.md`, whether or not the documentation file exists yet.
- Translate application outcomes into safe client-relevant details. Unexpected defects use an explicit generic-server problem type and never expose stack traces, vendor failures, secrets, or implementation details.
- GraphQL request and execution errors retain GraphQL's standard response format, including syntax and validation failures returned with an HTTP error status. Preserve the required `errors` and applicable `data` entries, put application-specific error metadata in `extensions`, and apply the same safe-detail and information-disclosure rules.
- HTTP and GraphQL schemas are adapter contracts distinct from application and domain types. While WallpaperDB has no production or external consumers, breaking changes may update a contract and all of its usages, tests, and generated schemas together; do not introduce versioning until consumers require independent migration.

## Persistence adapters

- Reinforce domain invariants susceptible to concurrent or external writes with native persistence constraints. Translate constraint failures into application outcomes and use optimistic concurrency where mutable state could otherwise be silently overwritten. Complex domain policy does not belong in database triggers or procedures.

Transaction mechanics follow the [application's declared atomicity](application-and-domain.md#ports-and-transactions). Persistence and immutable-asset ownership follow [backend architecture](project-organization.md#backend-architecture). Committing a state change with an event also requires [delivery reliability](distributed-interactions.md#delivery-reliability).

## Testing

- Driving-adapter contract tests prove that external requests or messages become the correct driving-port calls and that every declared driving-port outcome or typed failure becomes the correct external response. Test protocol translation at this boundary.
- Driven-adapter contract tests run a port's behavioral contract against the production adapter and real infrastructure. Test infrastructure semantics at this boundary.

Apply the [shared testing principles](project-organization.md#shared-testing-principles). When testing composition rather than an adapter's contract, use [composition tests](composition-and-operations.md#testing). Instrumentation follows the separate [telemetry testing policy](composition-and-operations.md#testing).

## Problem

Profile editing components each manage mutation coordination, query ownership, stale responses, and focus lifetimes. Correctness depends on repeated guards spread across inline fields, picture settings, and alias settings. The existing tests cover many cases, but adding another editing flow requires understanding the same concurrency rules in several places.

This is a maintenance concern identified during #235, not a newly reproduced user-facing failure.

## Scope

Design a small Profile editing interface that owns the common mutation and owner-cache lifecycle. Move shared behavior behind it incrementally, preserving context-specific commands and presentation in each component. Keep DOM focus behavior close to the UI where it depends on actual user interaction; do not build a generic form framework.

Start with one editing flow, prove the interface through behavior tests, then migrate the picture and alias flows only where they share the same rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- Signing out, switching owners, or removing/recreating an owner query cannot let a late mutation restore stale Profile data or write into another owner's cache.
- Concurrent edits retain the existing serialization/version-conflict behavior. Failures preserve recoverable drafts and give the user an explicit next action.
- Navigation/unmount during a successful mutation updates only the still-valid owner cache and does not restore an obsolete component's focus.
- Dialog cancellation, retry, keyboard submission, and focus restoration preserve current behavior and respect intervening user focus changes.
- Components consume a deliberate public interface instead of repeating query-identity and mutation-coordination guards. Avoid wrappers whose interface merely reproduces the component's existing complexity.
- Existing behavioral regressions remain green, new guarantees have focused tests, and the deployed Profile editing flows pass browser validation.

## Starting points

- `apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-inline-field.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-picture-settings.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/profile/profile-alias-settings.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/hooks/use-owner-profile.ts`
- `apps/web/test/components/profile-bootstrap.test.tsx` and the related Profile component tests

Preserve Profile API contracts, displayed behavior, and the current owner-clearing guarantees. Select the exact module placement after examining the existing hooks and cache helpers.

## Parent

#243

## What to build

A signed-in User chooses a static JPEG, PNG, or WebP in the existing Profile picture dialog, frames it in a square crop, and applies the change. Browser processing produces the small canonical image before upload while the page remains responsive and cancellable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reuse the existing dialog. Source selection changes its contents into the editor; processing never opens another modal.
- [ ] Fetch the effective User picture policy before processing. Validate supported source formats with a clear error; do not reject a local static source solely because of compressed file size or megapixel count.
- [ ] Offer a fixed 1:1 crop, drag positioning, an accessible keyboard-operable zoom slider, and Reset. Display a circular preview mask while exporting a square asset without baked-in circular clipping.
- [ ] Clamp movement so the source covers the entire crop at every allowed zoom and position. Preserve transparent source pixels without adding padding outside the source bounds.
- [ ] Cap zoom before the selected crop represents less than 64 by 64 source pixels. If its initial region is already smaller, disable further zoom, show a quality warning, and still allow Apply.
- [ ] Selecting a replacement unsaved source replaces the previous selection immediately and resets crop and zoom without a confirmation dialog.
- [ ] Apply source orientation before editing/cropping. Produce a predictable sRGB SDR WebP at the policy's canonical dimensions, initially 512 by 512, with static encoding starting at quality 85. Preserve alpha and strip private and unrelated source metadata.
- [ ] Perform decode and transformation outside the main UI thread when supported. A fallback yields sufficiently for cancellation and UI updates to remain responsive.
- [ ] Show a small loader and accessible X cancel button inside the same dialog during processing. Cancellation stops outstanding processing and prevents partial or late processing results from being uploaded.
- [ ] Apply processes and uploads only the canonical result through the dedicated authenticated picture command, independent of unrelated Profile saves. Never upload or retain the large original.
- [ ] Close the dialog only after User accepts the upload and publish the accepted authoritative Profile response. Decode, processing, and upload failures show a clear error and retain source and crop for another attempt.
- [ ] Release UI-owned worker work and object URLs when appropriate. A superseded selection or abandoned editing session cannot receive a late processing result or submit the wrong source.
- [ ] Preserve the existing nested confirmation for picture removal and generated-avatar selection. Do not introduce rotation, flipping, arbitrary aspect ratios, forced camera capture, or a general form refactor.

## Blocked by

- #337 - Expose effective Profile picture policy and enforce canonical static uploads

## Testing

- Use a complete static browser E2E journey through the actual editor, worker, upload command, and updated Profile picture. Cover pointer positioning, keyboard slider control, Reset, and browser-dependent cancellation.
- Use focused public-interface tests for crop geometry, clamping, minimum source-region zoom, and the below-64-pixel case.
- Frontend adapter tests cover source replacement, policy/decode/processing/upload failures, retained edits, outgoing processed bytes and expected version, and late completion after cancellation or session replacement.
- Use real fixtures to verify orientation, transparency, metadata removal, canonical dimensions, and sRGB SDR output. Use bounded completion waits without fixed sleeps or retries that hide failure.

## Scope

This is an approved implementation slice of #243. It produces one canonical SDR Profile picture Asset and preserves User ownership, immutable identity, current-picture availability, and the existing removal/import lifecycle. Generic Media rendition delivery and HDR conversion are separate work. The accepted HDR policy in #270 and its Media processing ownership leave this SDR browser path intact; neither that work nor #237 is an additional blocker unless listed explicitly.

## Parent

#39

## What to build

Let a signed-in User change their Profile Handle while preserving link continuity. The User service atomically claims the normalized Handle, enforces reserved names and the seven-day cooldown, turns the previous Handle into an alias, and projects canonical routing changes to GraphQL and web.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Handle changes use the explicit authenticated command and optimistic Profile version.
- [ ] Handles enforce lowercase ASCII letters, digits, single hyphens, configurable 1–30 length, and technical reserved names.
- [ ] Current Handles and aliases share one unique PostgreSQL claim namespace.
- [ ] Concurrent claims permit exactly one winner and assign a monotonically increasing claim generation.
- [ ] A successful change makes the previous current Handle an alias and records all transitions atomically.
- [ ] A Profile cannot change Handle more than once per seven days.
- [ ] Old and new public routes resolve and redirect to the new canonical Handle after projection.
- [ ] Settings explain validation, collision, cooldown, and successful redirect behavior.
- [ ] Tests cover normalization, reserved names, concurrency, cooldown, events, projection, and redirects.

## Blocked by

- #166

## Parent

#39

## What to build

Let users discover Profiles through fuzzy Handle, active-alias, and Display name search, then select a Profile in the wallpaper filter UI to run an exact Profile-ID wallpaper query. Keep Profile data in the Profile index rather than denormalizing it into wallpaper documents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GraphQL exposes cursor-paginated Profile search over current Handles, active/expiring aliases, and Display names.
- [ ] Ranking prioritizes exact current Handle, Handle prefix, exact alias, alias prefix, Display name phrase/prefix, then fuzzy Display name.
- [ ] Current Handles outrank aliases and Profile ID is a stable pagination tiebreaker.
- [ ] Biography is not searched and public Profile results do not enumerate alias lists.
- [ ] If duplicate projected claims appear, exact resolution chooses the highest claim generation.
- [ ] The web filter provides fuzzy Profile selection and stores/submits the selected Profile ID.
- [ ] Wallpaper filtering remains an exact ownership-ID query; Profile fields are not copied into wallpaper documents.
- [ ] Tests cover ranking, aliases through expiry, cursor stability, duplicate claims, selection UX, and wallpaper results.

## Blocked by

- #172
- #173
- #169

## Parent PRD

#35

## What to build

Migrate the gateway's pagination from offset-based (`from`/`size`) to OpenSearch's `search_after` cursor-based pagination. The public GraphQL API remains unchanged — cursors stay opaque (HMAC-signed base64url) — but internally they encode `search_after` values instead of integer offsets.

For unsorted queries, use `search_after: [wallpaperId]` as a deterministic tiebreaker. Update `CursorService` to encode/decode an array of values (strings, numbers) instead of a single offset integer. Update `WallpaperRepository.search()` to accept `searchAfter` instead of `from`. Update the resolver to pass `search_after` values from decoded cursors and encode new cursors from the last result's sort values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CursorService` encodes/decodes `search_after` values (array) instead of integer offsets
- [ ] `WallpaperRepository.search()` uses `search_after` instead of `from`/`size`
- [ ] Resolver passes `search_after` from decoded cursor and encodes new cursors from result sort values
- [ ] Forward pagination (`first` + `after`) works correctly
- [ ] Backward pagination (`last` + `before`) works correctly
- [ ] Unsorted queries use `search_after: [wallpaperId]` for deterministic ordering
- [ ] Public GraphQL API is unchanged — cursors remain opaque to clients
- [ ] Existing integration tests updated and passing
- [ ] HMAC signing and cursor expiration still enforced

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

## User stories addressed

- User story 10
